chapter: New York, Nick's and the Army
title: The Pick magazine article and his miserable basic training
summary: A Pick magazine story on his Commodore sessions gets pinned up at camp, earning him every dirty job; he calls himself the world's worst soldier.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well, then, when you went into the Army you had already had behind you the Commodore records - they were freshly out--- most of them - there were more to come. You had been playing in the Town Hall concert with Eddie Condon and everybody else - then Ernie Anderson started - right?
Oh, yeah - I was doing everything -- man, I was making money and happy as hell--- you know.
In other words, you were getting pretty much of a reputation by this time.
Oh, sure -- but, you know, there was a guy named Carlton Brown---

--who had covered that record session for PICK MAGAZINE - he wrote for PICK and, uh, the unfortunate thing is I got the picture story - all about Wild Bill and all the pictures and all the things and the Commodore records and all the things -- and the story broke at a very bad time for me, because I was sent to Camp Virginia, sargeant Patrick Henry, and a smart-ass saw this and stuck it up on the bulletin board and said -- fellows- we have a real

celebrity among us. And, you know, in the Army this is a bad scene. So, I got every dirty job there was to get in the Army -- I got it -- just through that article--- and, uh, I played like hell in the Army. I did a lot of things and a lot of playing---
That's the main thing you did do - right?
That's all I did. I played--- I had my own Dixie Land Jazz Band---
So, these dirty jobs that you were talking about - that was just getting through the basic training---

Yeah, the basic part. It was really hard for me. Gee, I had never done all this kind of exercise and double times and oh, gee, I don't want to tell you about my Army career because I really hated it--- it was just that I was undoubtedly the world's worst soldier and they told me as much when I got out of the Army but I played a lot; I went down to Asheville and I think I had such a good band in Asheville where I was stationed - North Carolina--- that the Army authorized my band so I had a real authorized Dixie Land Jazz Band in the United State Army---
